webhooks.summary: The provided Datadog OpenAPI content includes webhook-management operations for two distinct surfaces: (1) Microsoft Teams 'Workflows webhook handles' and (2) the Webhooks integration's OAuth2 client-credentials auth methods. However, the source material does NOT define any inbound webhook event names (webhookEventNames is an empty array), provides no webhook payload/definition sample, declares no operation callbacks, and documents no signature headers or verification scheme. As a result, event names, signature headers, and verification schemes are reported as empty/unknown below — no values are inferred.

setupSteps.title: Retrieve Datadog API/APP key credentials
setupSteps.detail: Obtain a valid Datadog API key and Application key for authenticating calls to /api/v2/integration/... endpoints.

setupSteps.title: Register an OAuth2 client-credentials auth method (only if your inbound target requires OAuth2)
setupSteps.detail: POST /api/v2/integration/webhooks/configuration/auth-method/oauth2-client-credentials with the client credentials Datadog should use when calling your webhook URL. Persist the returned auth_method_id.

setupSteps.title: Manage Microsoft Teams Workflows webhook handles (only for the MS Teams integration surface)
setupSteps.detail: POST /api/v2/integration/ms-teams/configuration/workflows-webhook-handles to create a Workflows webhook handle, or GET/PATCH the collection to inspect and update handles.

setupSteps.title: Register the inbound hook URL in the Datadog Webhooks integration
setupSteps.detail: The provided source material does NOT include the endpoint that creates or registers an actual webhook target URL for the generic Datadog Webhooks integration (only auth-method and MS Teams handle management operations are present). Without that endpoint visible in the source, this final registration step cannot be made actionable from the supplied OpenAPI content alone — complete it in the Datadog Webhooks configuration area once the webhook-creation endpoint is available.
